## Gap

batter-7r3.8 lets owned fixtures construct pools that authenticate as a separately provisioned login (PlannedPool::password_login). Session policy can only be applied through public native hooks (PgSessionProfile::reset_and_apply in after_connect/after_release). PgProfiledPool and RunledgerDatabase cannot host a fixture-managed pool, and PgProfiledPool's before_acquire verify_idle hook is crate-private, so a fixture pool cannot reproduce the application's full three-hook profiled pool or hand out a PgProfiledPool/RunledgerDatabase handle that the fixture driver closes.

## Direction

Let a planned fixture pool be declared with a PgSessionProfile so the fixture constructs it through PgProfiledPool::connect_lazy (all three hooks owned by the library, no replaceable setup callback) after login resolution, registers it before the first connectivity check, and closes it before lease cleanup. Compose with batter-nhu5's single profiled pool owner rather than adding a second one.

## Evidence

ADR-010 'Fixture login pool assessment (batter-7r3.8)'; bead comment 391 on batter-7r3.8 (consumer A's close-aware adapter).
fields.acceptance_criteria: A fixture-declared profiled pool (lease or password login) is constructed through the library-owned three-hook path, registered before the first connectivity check and closed before lease cleanup; live tests prove profile verification on acquisition and retained failures; no replaceable hook or second pool owner is introduced; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.

## Outcome

An application that installs `redacting_panic_hook` can also get a structured, payload-free record of each panic in its log pipeline, without any code that can panic or block running inside the panic hook.

## Evidence

- ADR-014's survey: consumers B and C route panics into their structured logs today (by formatting `PanicHookInfo`, which discloses the payload). Moving them to `redacting_panic_hook` removes panic events from those logs. That meets the two-consumer threshold for a shared need.
- `batter-4q78` design review (2026-11-02, throwaway experiments, not repository tests): the idiomatic wrapper, a `take_hook` chain around `tracing::error!`, either discloses the payload again or, in a location-only form, turns a caught task panic into SIGABRT when the log pipe is closed. tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 reports its own write failures with `eprintln!`, which panics on a closed pipe, and std aborts on any panic raised while a hook runs (`MustAbort::PanicInHook`); `catch_unwind` inside the hook cannot contain it. No test can make subscriber code inside a hook abort-safe; only deferral avoids it.

## Candidate design (proposed, unexecuted)

- The hook keeps its stderr line and also copies the panic site into a fixed-capacity, allocation-free slot or ring (the file into a bounded byte buffer, because `Location`'s borrow ends with the hook), with a dropped-entry count.
- A registered Batter component drains the slot outside the hook and emits a `batter`-target event with file, line, column and the dropped count.
- Documented limit: an uncaught panic in `main` exits before the drain, so the stderr line remains the evidence there.

## Non-goals

Emitting `tracing` events or formatting anything inside the hook; panic classification or recovery; installing a hook from library code.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- A dead log pipe and a panicking or re-entrant subscriber never abort the process or block the panicking thread; a subprocess test proves it.
- No payload is reachable from the emitted event; a subprocess test with a secret-shaped payload proves it.
- The ADR-010 invalid-state review, guarantees, operations wording, status row, rustdoc and example are updated, and bash scripts/verify.sh passes.
fields.title: Structured panic events emitted outside the panic hook

data.text: Design (2026-11-02, branch feat/redacting-panic-hook-4q78): batter_core::redacting_panic_hook() -> Box<dyn Fn(&PanicHookInfo<'_>) + Send + Sync + 'static>, #[must_use], root re-export (batter::redacting_panic_hook). Renderer takes only file/line/column; one line 'a thread panicked at <loc>; panic payload redacted' in one write through a dup of fd 2 (try_clone_to_owned). Decisions after a five-lens design critique (API invalid-state, std/Tokio source check on 1.98.1, test evidence, docs/policy, fresh-agent usability): no thread name (thread::current panics after runtime cleanup -> abort inside a hook); never take the Stderr lock, including as a fallback (lock held inside eprint! can block indefinitely; experiment reproduced a deadlock), so at the descriptor limit the hook writes nothing; contract says 'never reads, writes or forwards' because std formats panic! args before any hook; std still prints a constant nested message on PanicInHook and the full payload in a forked child before exec; closing the dup releases POSIX fcntl record locks. No witness/install() API: std cannot report the installed hook without replacing it. Hook installed first in all 9 facade examples plus reference-service main, retire_startup_controls, postgres-lifecycle main and the single-facade consumer; reference_preflight and single_facade_harness (test tooling) keep the default hook. Rustdoc pointers on Command::start_with_unix_signals, Startup::with_unix_signals, service::start. Follow-up for structured payload-free panic events outside the hook: batter-krpp. Locked-dependency scan: only ratatui 0.30.2 init/try_init/run chain the hook (unused); proc-macro2 swaps only under cfg(no_is_available).

Earlier full runs on intermediate trees also passed; one run aborted only because new files were intent-to-add (git add -N), which the file-budget checker refuses. Targets: unit 5 tests; tests/panic_hook.rs 8 parent tests + child_fixture, 10 children; panic_hook_ownership 4 tests (15 Batter-consuming roots checked, 3 tooling roots, 12 native roots). Mutation checks (temporary edits, restored, not committed), each caught: hook writes payload (6 failures); hook writes only &'static str payloads (caught case fails); hook takes Stderr lock (lock-held + descriptor-limit fail); old lock fallback (descriptor-limit fails); entrypoint replaces / wraps hook (runtime sentinel test and static scan both fail); a consumer root loses its install (inventory fails). Review: five-lens design critique, then a 4-dimension diff review with one skeptic per finding (22 confirmed, all fixed), then a resolution check plus fresh critic (further fixes: benchmark as named tooling root, complete classified inventory, checked-in scope, ScopedStartup/DeferredScopedStartup names, usage/facade-row scope, libtest take_hook nuance). fields.description:
## Outcome

Outbound provider calls run through one library-owned, send-once HTTP exchange. The library builds the client (no redirects, no automatic replay, no ambient proxy discovery, a required connect timeout, HTTP/1.1), refuses to start once the caller's deadline is too close, derives the transport timeout from that deadline, bounds the response body under the same deadline, and returns an exhaustive outcome: not started, not dispatched (connector failure), unknown, or responded with the status retained. Its values and errors carry no URL, query, credential or body. Provider meaning, replay, idempotency, fences and reconciliation stay with applications.

## Evidence (read-only three-consumer survey, 2026-11-02; consumer identities and paths stay outside this tracker)

- All three applications hand-write the same transport rule: a connector failure proves that the attempt wrote no request bytes, any later failure leaves the outcome unknown, and a received status line is a response. The same rule appears in an owner-maintained billing library, in batter-otlp's private transport and in the reference service.
- Repairs: Consumer C needed about twelve dispatch-evidence repairs within three days, hand-copied URL stripping across 22 endpoints until a lint banned direct sends, and retrofitted start-before-deadline gates into 27 gateway methods. Consumer B lost a received status when the body stalled, and the fix was copied between provider crates. Consumer A needed four configurations to nest its transport timer inside the retry attempt cap. The billing library repaired its status-to-certainty mapping repeatedly.
- Client settings have drifted. One of C's clients disables redirects but leaves reqwest's HTTP/2 protocol-NACK replay live through feature unification, honours proxy environment variables, sets no connect timeout and leaves a credential header unmarked. A reads response bodies without a bound.
- Upstream (reqwest 0.13.x, hyper-util 0.1.20, read from source): hyper-util assigns its Connect kind only to connector or checkout failures, before the request is handed to a connection. reqwest's Display includes the full URL with its query, it has no response size limit, and its default redirect policy replays bodies and custom credential headers cross-host on 307/308.
- B's provider crates forbid any dependency named batter*, so B is evidence of need, not an adopter.

## Scope

- A new standalone package `batter-outbound`: no batter-core dependency by default, and an opt-in `operation` feature that bridges `OperationContext` deadlines and cancellation. The facade re-exports it as `batter::outbound` behind an opt-in `outbound` feature.
- This is a focused experimental extraction (ADR-014 track 1). A new ADR records why transport evidence differs from the generic provider interface ADR-014 rejected.
- A validated origin (HTTPS, or HTTP to a literal loopback address), segment-confined paths, request headers marked sensitive by construction, request preparation that surfaces every builder failure before an exchange exists, one consuming send, a bounded body and a closed outcome.

## Non-goals

Provider adapters or traits, status-to-meaning helpers, retry or replay, idempotency keys, Retry-After, dispatch fences, reconciliation, token caches, request signing, webhook ingress, HTTP/2, and operator-supplied destinations.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Loopback fault tests pin every outcome: a refused connection is not dispatched; an expired deadline or cancellation before start is not started and the peer sees no connection; a lost response, a stalled head and cancellation in flight are unknown; a stalled, truncated or oversized body is a response with its status retained; a redirect is returned, not followed; no case sends more than one request.
- No URL, query, header value or body appears in any Debug or Display output, checked with marker values.
- Rustdoc and a runnable facade example. The new ADR, the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment, guarantees, status, references and CHANGELOG are updated, and `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.
fields.title: Send provider calls through a library-owned send-once HTTP exchange with exhaustive transport evidence

## Outcome

Native Runledger never persists or logs a caught handler panic payload. A handler panic records the static `job.handler_panic` code with a fixed message.

## Evidence

`runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs:586-593` formats the caught payload into the `JobFailure` message (`"Job handler panicked: {payload}"`). That message is persisted in `job_queue.last_error_message`, `job_attempts.error_message`, `job_dead_letters.error_message` and the `job_events` payload. It is logged at warn on dead-letter (`runledger-runtime/src/worker/completion.rs:187-205`) and shown in the TUI. Payloads from `unwrap` and `expect` carry the Debug of the error; a reqwest error's Debug includes the full URL. This bypasses the redaction that `redacting_panic_hook` gives the hook's own output, and docs/operations.md does not list the exception. Existing tests assert only the failure code. Found during the 2026-11-02 consumer survey; no surveyed consumer depends on the text.

## Scope

- A fixed message for handler panics. The code and the PANICKED kind stay unchanged.
- Optionally, a static message for the serde arm of `From<JobExecutionError>`.
- Rustdoc on `JobFailure` constructors stating that messages are persisted verbatim and must not carry error Display or Debug text.

## Non-goals

Changing `JobFailure` constructor or field types (a native hard cut; it stays on the watch list).
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- A PostgreSQL-backed runtime test panics with a secret-bearing formatted payload, then asserts that the marker is absent from job_queue, job_attempts, job_dead_letters, the job_events payload and the dead-letter log, while the code and kind are unchanged.
- A Runledger CHANGELOG "Changed" entry and docs/operations.md updated; `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.
fields.title: Keep caught handler panic payloads out of native Runledger failure records

fields.description:
## Outcome

`OperationContext` gains two additive APIs:
- `run_tracked`, whose exhaustive result separates an opaque, library-constructed `NotStarted` (the factory was never invoked) from an interruption after start;
- `child_until(Instant)`, a child bounded by the earlier of its parent's deadline and the instant, inheriting cancellation.

`run` and its precedence (cancellation, then deadline, then completion) stay unchanged.

## Evidence (read-only three-consumer survey, 2026-11-02; consumer identities and paths stay outside this tracker)

- Consumer C hand-writes a pre-poll gate that reports NotStarted versus Elapsed in six helpers and about 25 sites, because `run` reports both as `Interrupted(DeadlineExceeded)`.
- Consumer A records an attempt refused before start as a definite failure, and converts externally observed absolute deadlines into contexts by hand; `child(Duration)` reports an expired budget as a configuration error.
- Consumer B deliberately treats every interruption as unknown and does not need this.
- Precedents: `BlockingError::NotAdmitted` versus `Abandoned`; batter-runlimit hand-writes `InterruptedCheck::{NotStarted, InFlight}` on top of `run`.
- The two survey reviewers split (watch versus promote-narrowed). Deliver alongside or after the outbound exchange, and adopt `run_tracked` in the reference service dispatch as the consumer contract.

## Non-goals

- Changing `run`'s precedence, or a completion-first option for arbitrary futures: polling after the deadline can start new effects.
- A minimum-remaining start floor, and retry-level in-flight evidence (watch list).
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Paused-time tests: pre-cancelled and pre-expired contexts return NotStarted without invoking the factory; an interruption after start returns Interrupted; `child_until` never extends its parent and an elapsed instant yields an expired child.
- compile_fail doctests pin the private NotStarted constructor and the absence of From conversions.
- Rustdoc, the ADR-010 assessment, guarantees and CHANGELOG are updated, and `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.
fields.title: Report factory-not-started separately from interruption, and bound children by an absolute deadline

data.text: Decision 2026-11-02: placement is a standalone leaf package crates/batter-outbound (batter-at-rest precedent): no batter-core dependency by default; the opt-in 'operation' feature adds PreparedRequest::send_in(&OperationContext, ResponseLimit); the facade will re-export it as batter::outbound behind an opt-in 'outbound' feature. reqwest 0.13.5 (rustls), HTTP/1.1 only. Core source implemented on branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a (uncommitted): Origin, ConnectTimeout, ResponseLimit, Client (fixed profile: no redirects, referer off, retry::never, no_proxy, http1_only, no decompression, no hickory, 4 s pool idle, TLS>=1.2), RequestDraft/prepare (sensitive headers, reserved framing headers, dot/empty segments refused), PreparedRequest::send, exhaustive Exchange {NotStarted, NotDispatched, Unknown, Responded}. Deadline: RESERVE 50 ms + MINIMUM_ATTEMPT 50 ms; one package-owned timer bounds head and body; reqwest's per-request timeout is not used, so deadline reasons come from the package clock. Ready results win over a simultaneous timer/cancellation inside the exchange only. Local checks so far: cargo build, clippy (-D warnings -D clippy::mod_module_files) with and without 'operation', 2 sanity tests and 7 doctests pass. Tests, ADR-015, ADR-010 assessment, contracts and facade wiring in progress.

Progress 2026-11-02: build-out done by four parallel agents (tests, ADR-015 + ADR-010 assessment, contracts/package docs, facade + scripts wiring). Two implementation defects found in review and fixed: (1) url parsing deletes tab/LF/CR inside path segments before applying dot-segment rules, so a segment like '.<TAB>.' became '..' and removed a path level; prepare now refuses such segments (PrepareError::ControlCharacter) and checks that every segment survives normalization; (2) a URL that http::Uri rejects (e.g. over the http crate's length limit) passed prepare and was refused by reqwest at execution, reported as Unknown for a never-sent request; prepare now refuses it (PrepareError::InvalidUri) and Origin refuses hosts http::Uri rejects. Evidence additions: dev-dependency compiles reqwest gzip+http2 into test builds; tls_hello test (ALPN offers only http/1.1, TLS 1.2/1.3), gzip, idle-pool (4 s) and the new refusals are mutation-verified (each fails when its setting is removed). 60+ integration tests, unit test for sensitive outgoing headers, compile_fail doctests for send-once. Full scripts/verify.sh run 1 started; adversarial six-dimension review running.

fields.description:
## Outcome

An owner decision records whether the experimental `batter-outbound` package ships in the first crates.io release train, and if so where it sits in the publish order.

## Evidence

- The facade declares `batter-outbound` as an optional dependency behind its `outbound` feature. Cargo requires optional dependencies to be published, so publishing `batter` with that dependency makes `batter-outbound` a mandatory upload before `batter`. Its own optional `operation` feature depends on `batter-core`, so it publishes after `batter-core`.
- The publication dossier (docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, `batter-ddc`) predates the package: its tier list, name-availability check, package count and dry runs do not include it.
- ADR-014 track 2 applies two-consumer evidence to the APIs proposed for release. ADR-015 records the package as a focused experimental extraction with no adopting application root yet.

## Scope

- Name-availability check for `batter-outbound` on crates.io.
- Tier placement (after `batter-core`, before `batter`) and a packaging dry run.
- The owner's decision: ship it experimental in the first train, as `batter-otlp` is, or hold the facade's `outbound` feature until promotion.

## Non-goals

Publishing anything. This records evidence and a decision only.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The dossier or its successor lists batter-outbound with its name check, tier placement and dry-run result, and the owner's ship-or-hold decision is recorded; nothing is published.
fields.title: Record a release-train decision for the experimental batter-outbound package

data.text: Review round 1 (six adversarial reviewers, 96 findings, 0 blocker, 32 major) applied. Code: (1) TLS moved off reqwest's rustls feature (aws-lc-rs) to rustls-no-provider + a package-built rustls ClientConfig: explicit ring provider, TLS 1.3/1.2, OS verifier for HTTPS, empty root store for loopback HTTP (loopback clients never read the host store), ALPN http/1.1 set by the package; lockfile has no aws-lc-rs again, removing the two-provider panic hazard for default-provider rustls builders (bollard over TLS Docker, hyper-rustls helpers). (2) NotStarted/NotDispatched are now opaque, package-constructed evidence (compile_fail,E0451); Unknown stays constructible. (3) Segments whose part before ';' is empty or a dot segment are refused. (4) Body buffer growth bounded by the limit and shrunk before return. (5) Rustdoc: RESERVE is not a recording budget; cancelled contexts record nothing; version contract (lockfile versions, manifest ^0.13.5, hyper/hyper-util unconstrained); macOS verifier blocking (source-inspected); Unknown may arrive late; undelimited bodies; Tokio time requirement. (6) Facade example rewritten: explicit pre-send fence step, Option<Fence> when parent cancelled, refusing port kept bound, clients built before budgets, 7 tests incl. 201-with-unusable-body and in-flight parent cancellation. (7) Matrix: outbound tests run alone in their batch. New tests: trust_store (Linux; ClientError::Build executed with SSL_CERT_FILE=/dev/null), body-phase cancellation/timer tie, undelimited body, ';' cases, one-request checks on tie tests. Manual mutation checks (each restored): ALPN line, no_gzip, idle 4s->90s, control-char check, body select swap, loopback verifier -> each fails its test; http1_only removal now fails none (defence in depth behind the explicit ALPN). Verify run 1 stopped at the single-facade consumer because /home ran out of disk (No space left on device); 51 GB of incremental caches under target/ were removed; everything before that point passed. Docs reconciliation running. Follow-up filed: batter-nt44 (release-train decision).

Verification 2026-11-02 (uncommitted working tree on branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a, base f458679; Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.1 pinned): CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 bash scripts/verify.sh passed, exit 0. Covered fmt, file budget (2 notices, 0 warnings), all four clippy configurations, every test_matrix part (workspace-tests 486 s; no-default-features with outbound-library in batch 1 and outbound-tests alone in batch 2; doctests; consumers incl. facade-feature-controls with the outbound feature/negative case and the single-facade consumer; runlimit; scripts), rustdoc -D warnings and all HTTP smoke profiles. CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 was used only to stay within disk after run 1 hit 'No space left on device'; no script reads it. Package suites: 64 tests with --all-features and 10 doctests (3 compile_fail with codes E0451/E0599/E0382); facade example 7 tests; example main prints 'mutation exchange: responded' and 'closed-port exchange: not_dispatched.connect_failed'. Not executed anywhere: macOS, DNS failure, TCP-phase connect timeout, pool checkout failure, stale keep-alive race, HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY for https origins, dropped send future, non-empty chunk tie, http1_only/retry/referer/brotli/zstd/deflate/hickory switches (defence in depth). Fresh-agent usability evaluation proposed, unexecuted. A final two-reviewer read-only pass is running.

Final review round (2 reviewers, 14 findings: 1 major, 7 minor, 6 nit) applied: Client rustdoc and manifest comment no longer claim the package adds no second rustls provider (it compiles rustls ring and reqwest rustls-no-provider; graphs that also compile aws-lc-rs, or that build other reqwest 0.13 clients with no TLS feature, need the root to install a process default) and mark each profile setting tested or defence in depth; tls_hello now asserts no process-default provider is installed after a handshake; the example's finalization result is matched exhaustively (Interrupted -> None, Failed(Infallible) unreachable) instead of .ok(); budget test widened to 599 ms; RESERVE/send_in docs carry the macOS blocking-poll exception; SECURITY.md names both library-built clients (batter-otlp, batter-outbound); feature-set-under-test claims scoped to the verification matrix (the standalone example command is the one that executes the shipped rustls-no-provider-only set); hyper-util idle eviction source recorded. Final verification on the final tree: CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 bash scripts/verify.sh, exit 0 (rustc 1.98.1, Linux x86_64; workspace-tests 452 s, outbound-tests 9 s, facade-feature-controls and single-facade-consumer passed). Nothing committed; work is on branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a. Leaving the bead claimed until the owner decides on commit/PR.

Review-fix loop (jig-review, controller run 53653559-8de0-4fa0-a388-7eaed4ce3dab, host claude, balanced policy, fix mode balanced, commit mode per-round): CONVERGED at round 0. The controller checkpointed the delivery as commit 76d71d7 'feat(outbound): add a send-once outbound HTTP exchange' on branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a (parent f458679; not pushed). Two independent Claude reviews of f458679..76d71d7 reported no findings and marked outcomes, redaction, profile, preparation, evidence and docs satisfied; verification was settled by controller receipts on the same fingerprint: 00008-validate 'env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 bash scripts/verify.sh' exit 0, 00009-validate 'python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_*.py' exit 0 (178 tests, 1 skipped); prerequisites cargo/rustc 1.98.1, Python 3.12.3, Docker passed. No repair round was needed. Remaining before close: push and PR/merge on the owner's request.
Pushed branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a (76d71d7) and opened PR #77 against master: https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/77. Hosted CI has not completed at the time of this comment.

PR #77 panel review (Claude + Codex, scope f458679..76d71d7) found four low findings, now repaired in review-fix run b9db8a72 round 1 (validation and fresh review pending): (1) docs/usage.md snippet discarded finalization errors via .ok() -> exhaustive match like the facade example (compiled on 1.98.1 in a scratch crate); (2) verification never executed the shipped reqwest selection -> new no-default-features batch outbound-shipped-features runs 'cargo test -p batter --no-default-features --features outbound --example outbound_exchange --locked' (cargo tree with dev edges: reqwest features rustls-no-provider/__rustls/__tls only; 7 tests pass locally), runner controls now 30 commands, docs updated; (3) 'no telemetry is emitted' replaced by 'adds no instrumentation of its own' plus a source-inspected audit of the locked shipped graph: only reqwest + rustls-platform-verifier (log) and hyper-util (tracing) emit events; reqwest debug host, hyper-util authority/socket addresses at debug/trace, verifier error-level failure with expected/presented names; none formats an exchange path/query/header/body; hyper built without tracing, rustls without logging; disclosed in lib.rs, README, SECURITY.md, ADR-010, operations, guarantees, status, CHANGELOG, references; (4) provider-default test wording now 'building the client and sending a ClientHello; no test completes a handshake'. No runtime or public API change.

fields.title: test_jig_integration fails intermittently: Jig 0.7.1 cannot confirm git child process-group cleanup under host process churn
fields.description: scripts/test_jig_integration.py fails intermittently because the pinned Jig 0.7.1 file-budget binary (scripts/jig -> .git/jig-tools/release-0.7.1-contract-8-runtime) reports 'Failed to run git <rev-parse|diff|status|ls-files> ... in <repository>: the process tree could not be cleaned up safely' instead of the file-budget result the test asserts. Jig spawns each git child in its own process group and confirms cleanup by scanning /proc for live group members; the failure appears when host-wide process churn is high. Evidence from 2026-11-03 (PR #77 review-fix run ed8cbdc0): two full 'python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_*.py' runs in the loop's validation worker failed with 1 and 4 such errors, all in this module, while the other 179-182 tests passed; locally the module failed 1 of 6 plain runs and 1 of 3 runs in a worker-like setsid topology and passed in isolation. The host then carried ~7,700 processes, several fresh qemu VMs and a PID counter at pid_max (4194304), so PIDs were wrapping. scripts/verify.sh does not run this module (the scripts matrix part lists other test modules), so the repository gate is unaffected; broader script-suite runs are. No repository change in that range touched Jig paths.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The Jig file-budget integration tests pass reliably under concurrent host process churn, either through a Jig release whose process-group cleanup confirmation tolerates /proc churn and PID reuse, or a documented repository decision; no semantic assertion in test_jig_integration.py is weakened.

CI fixed on PR #77 (head 360eab7, 'test(scripts): keep two script tests independent of the Cargo cache'). fields.title: Rename batter-outbound to batter-outbound-http before its first release
fields.description: The experimental outbound exchange package (merged in PR #77) is named batter-outbound, with facade feature 'outbound' and module batter::outbound. The name omits HTTP, so an agent searching the facade for HTTP finds only the inbound Axum adapter, and 'outbound' alone suggests a delivery or outbox layer with retries, which the package deliberately is not. Rename before the first release (the name is unpublished on crates.io and no consumer depends on it): package and directory crates/batter-outbound-http, library batter_outbound_http, facade feature 'outbound-http', facade module batter::outbound_http. Type names, the example name outbound_exchange and the matrix labels stay.
fields.acceptance_criteria: No stale reference to batter-outbound, batter_outbound, batter::outbound or the facade feature 'outbound' remains outside history (.beads) ; Cargo.lock regenerated by Cargo; scripts/verify.sh passes on Rust 1.98.1; hosted CI passes on the PR; the change is recorded as not a public hard cut because the old names were never released.

fields.title: Own outbound HTTP connections and gate handoff and writes by the exchange deadline

data.text: Assessment: confirmed a library-owned transport gap. The first-poll gate and reqwest-owned pooled writer could progress one request after a stall; a consumer poll-order wrapper cannot cover both. Replaced normal reqwest transport with fresh owned TCP/TLS and low-level hyper HTTP/1 driven inside the exchange future. Immediate handoff gate plus plaintext and raw-TCP write/flush gates preserve readable-reply precedence without late writer resumption. Pre-handoff stop is NotStarted; setup errors/timeouts are NotDispatched by phase. Public API inventory: 197 to 197 entries, zero removed/added; signatures manually unchanged. No shim/cut. Focused outbound suites, deterministic queued/partial writer tests, TLS 1.2/1.3 rejection and trusting/readable-reply controls, Clippy and shipped-graph controls pass on Linux/Rust 1.98.1. Full required verification follows; no new macOS or hosted evidence.

Completed and verified on Linux x86_64 / Rust 1.98.1. bash scripts/verify.sh exited 0: formatting, unchanged file-budget policy, all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts (workspace/native PostgreSQL and runtime suites, minimal features and standalone outbound, doctests, external consumers/graphs, native Runlimit, script controls), rustdoc with warnings denied, and all five HTTP smoke profiles. No matrix rerun was performed. The final peer-close fixture adjustment additionally passed all 10 all-feature wire tests, package all-target/all-feature Clippy, formatting and file budgets; git diff --check is clean. Deterministic production-driver tests cover expired/cancelled handoff and queued/partial writer stalls, including no background progress while the exchange is unpolled. Real TLS 1.2/1.3 tests reject an untrusted certificate, pass a private trusting control and retain a readable body after expiry. Full/minimal suites and shipped facade graph controls pass; reqwest is dev-only, and the normal/shipped graphs reject its pool and hyper-util client-legacy. Cargo generated the lockfile dependency-list update with no version changes. Public API inventory is 197 to 197, zero additions/removals, with unchanged public signatures manually checked; evidence is docs/evidence/outbound-owned-connection-api-diff-2026-11-04.md. Contracts, ADR-010/015 assessment, reference sources, status, guides and changelog updated. Cooperative already-entered polls, kernel-accepted bytes, dropped-exchange uncertainty and application replay/reconciliation obligations remain explicit. No new macOS, public-CA acceptance, hosted execution, fresh-agent adoption or downstream deployment is claimed. Changes are uncommitted; no code commit, push or publication was requested or performed.
